# robots.txt for www.anonymised.io
#
# Strategy
#   1. Allow traditional search engines and AI search/citation crawlers full
#      access, except AI agents on client downloads (below).
#   2. Restrict AI training crawlers to the home page, /about-us and the
#      substantive content sections — this lets them shape model knowledge of
#      Anonymised without giving away bandwidth on forms and low-value paths.
#   3. Fully block bots with a track record of abusive crawling or negligible return.
#
# Client downloads (/resources/): search engines may fetch them, because that is
# how they see the X-Robots-Tag: noindex header. The named AI search and user
# agents are disallowed there; the AI training crawlers are already blocked.
# These are requests to crawlers, not access control.
#
# Last reviewed: 19 October 2026
# Source of truth: public/robots.txt in the website repository


# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Traditional search engines — full access
# Googlebot also feeds Google AI Overviews. Bingbot also feeds Microsoft Copilot.
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

User-agent: Googlebot
Allow: /

User-agent: Bingbot
Allow: /

User-agent: Applebot
Allow: /

User-agent: DuckDuckBot
Allow: /


# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# AI search / citation crawlers — full access except client downloads
# These fetch at query time and produce inline citations with referral traffic.
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# OpenAI — ChatGPT search results surface
User-agent: OAI-SearchBot
Allow: /
Disallow: /resources/

# OpenAI — fetches a URL when a ChatGPT user asks it to read one
User-agent: ChatGPT-User
Allow: /
Disallow: /resources/

# Anthropic — Claude's search citations (replaces the old Claude-Web)
User-agent: Claude-SearchBot
Allow: /
Disallow: /resources/

# Anthropic — fetches a URL when a Claude user asks it to read one
User-agent: Claude-User
Allow: /
Disallow: /resources/

# Perplexity — primary search crawler
User-agent: PerplexityBot
Allow: /
Disallow: /resources/

# Perplexity — user-initiated fetches
User-agent: Perplexity-User
Allow: /
Disallow: /resources/

# DuckDuckGo Assist (DuckAssist) — answer engine citations
User-agent: DuckAssistBot
Allow: /
Disallow: /resources/


# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# AI training crawlers — restricted to substantive public content
# These shape what foundation models "know" about Anonymised at inference time.
# Allow on the pages that should influence that knowledge (the home page and
# /about-us say what Anonymised is and does); block everywhere else
# to limit crawl volume and avoid leaking low-value pages into training sets.
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# OpenAI training
User-agent: GPTBot
Allow: /$
Allow: /about-us
Allow: /hub
Allow: /blog-posts
Allow: /products
Allow: /press-coverage
Disallow: /
Crawl-delay: 2

# Anthropic training
User-agent: ClaudeBot
Allow: /$
Allow: /about-us
Allow: /hub
Allow: /blog-posts
Allow: /products
Allow: /press-coverage
Disallow: /
Crawl-delay: 2

# Google — Gemini training + Vertex AI Grounding (does NOT affect AI Overviews,
# which use Googlebot)
User-agent: Google-Extended
Allow: /$
Allow: /about-us
Allow: /hub
Allow: /blog-posts
Allow: /products
Allow: /press-coverage
Disallow: /

# Apple Intelligence training (separate from Applebot, which handles search)

Allow: /$
Allow: /about-us
Allow: /hub
Allow: /blog-posts
Allow: /products
Allow: /press-coverage
Disallow: /

# Common Crawl — ingested by many third-party model trainers
User-agent: CCBot
Allow: /$
Allow: /about-us
Allow: /hub
Allow: /blog-posts
Allow: /products
Allow: /press-coverage

# Anonymised

> Anonymised is the audience layer between first-party data and the platforms where media is bought. It adds real-time open-web intent to the data advertisers and publishers already own, so advertisers get better results from the same spend and publishers get more revenue from the same inventory.

ID Ward Limited, trading as Anonymised. 7 Bell Yard, London WC2A 2JR.

## Products

- [AudienceLift](https://www.anonymised.io/products/audiencelift): For advertisers. AudienceLift enriches your first-party data with real open-web behaviour, builds audience personas and activates them across Meta, Google and programmatic.
- [SignalLift](https://www.anonymised.io/products/signallift): For publishers. SignalLift makes your first-party audience intelligence usable by open-market buyers in Google Ad Manager, lifting fill rate and revenue per impression.
- [Publisher Data Platform](https://www.anonymised.io/products/publisher-data-platform): For publishers. The Anonymised Publisher Data Platform turns your audience data, enriched with open-web behaviour, into personas built to an advertiser's brief.
- [Curation](https://www.anonymised.io/products/curation): For advertisers and publishers. Anonymised curation packages open-web audiences as programmatic deals on anonymised cohorts, reaching inventory that identifier-based targeting cannot price.

## Company

- [About us](https://www.anonymised.io/about-us): Anonymised is the audience layer between first-party data and the platforms where media is bought, adding real-time open-web intent to the data you own.
- [Hub](https://www.anonymised.io/hub): Product news, research and commentary from the Anonymised team, plus where we have appeared in the trade press.
- [Press coverage](https://www.anonymised.io/press-coverage): Anonymised in the trade press: coverage of our partnerships, product launches and views on privacy-first, agentic and programmatic advertising.
- [Book a demo](https://www.anonymised.io/demo): Book a 30-minute demo on your own data. Advertisers see the personas in their first-party data; publishers see SignalLift sized on their Ad Manager data.

## Blog

- [How to Protect Your Google Ads Data Before the Google Signals Changes Take Effect](https://www.anonymised.io/blog-posts/how-to-protect-your-google-ads-data-before-the-google-signals-changes-take-effect): Google retired the Google Signals safety net for consent-based tracking on June 15, 2026. What changed, and how to catch up if your setup still needs it.
- [Anonymised launches Audience Lift to transform first-party data into high-performance audiences](https://www.anonymised.io/blog-posts/anonymised-launches-audience-lift-to-transform-first-party-data-into-high-performance-audiences): Audience Lift enriches first-party data with live interest and intent signals to build audiences for Meta and Google Ads. An early campaign cut CPA by 35%.
- [Anonymised and Bytek partnership enables secure first-party data activation for expanded customer reach](https://www.anonymised.io/blog-posts/anonymised-and-bytek-partnership-enables-secure-first-party-data-activation-for-expanded-customer-reach): Anonymised and Bytek today announced a strategic partnership that marks a new step forward in the secure and predictive activation of first-party data.
- [Anonymised x Index: Custom Algorithms for ID-Less Ads](https://www.anonymised.io/blog-posts/anonymised-partners-with-index-exchange-to-enable-custom-algorithms-for-privacy-focused-id-less-targeting): Anonymised partners with Index Exchange, one of the largest independent SSPs, to run its custom algorithms natively within Index Marketplaces.
- [Anonymised and Bedrock: A New Era in ID-Less Advertising](https://www.anonymised.io/blog-posts/anonymised-bedrock-partnership-enables-accurate-id-less-targeting): Anonymised partners with Bedrock Platform, making its ID-less audiences natively available for buy-side targeting and measurement on premium inventory.
- [Anonymised x Onetag: High-Performance ID-Less Ads](https://www.anonymised.io/blog-posts/anonymised-partners-with-onetag-for-privacy-first-id-less-advertising): Anonymised and Onetag bring ID-less audience targeting and measurement to Onetag Smart Curation, across all browsers and devices, without third-party cookies.
- [Our CEO Mattia Fosci's comments on Meta and brand safety in ExchangeWire](https://www.anonymised.io/blog-posts/what-is-the-future-of-brand-safety-on-metas-platforms): Mattia Fosci on brand safety on Meta's platforms: why negative emotions erode brand trust, and why advertisers should turn to premium open-web publishers.
- [Our CEO Mattia Fosci's 2025 policy and regulation predictions in ExchangeWire](https://www.anonymised.io/blog-posts/2025-predictions-policy-regulation): Mattia Fosci's 2025 predictions for ad tech policy and regulation: big tech competition cases, the DMA and DSA, UK data law and US enforcement.
- [This is why publisher first-party data isn’t reaching its potential](https://www.anonymised.io/blog-posts/op-ed-the-id-bottleneck-this-is-why-publisher-first-party-data-isnt-reaching-its-potential): First-party data is still marginal in programmatic. Mattia Fosci argues the real problem is not the usual objections but the industry's addiction to ID.
- [Introducing Anonymised Frequency Capping](https://www.anonymised.io/blog-posts/introducing-anonymised-frequency-capping): Our latest feature to mitigate ad fatique whilst maximising ad spend efficiency in privacy compliant cookieless and ID-less programmatic advertising.
- [Introducing Anonymised Topics](https://www.anonymised.io/blog-posts/introducing-anonymised-topics): Anonymised Topics takes the guesswork out of turning a media brief into a high-performing targeting audience. Here is how it differs from Google Topics.
- [Why the industry is looking at ID-less advertising to fix its problems](https://www.anonymised.io/blog-posts/the-tyranny-of-the-matching-table-why-the-industry-is-looking-at-id-less-advertising-to-fix-its-problems): Why most cookieless alternatives are just cookies by another name, and why ID-less advertising offers a genuine way out of the matching-table trap.
- [The appeal of first-party data](https://www.anonymised.io/blog-posts/the-appeal-of-first-party-data): Will the end of third-party cookies really put first-party data at the centre of digital marketing? Allan Tinkler questions an assumption the industry makes.
- [Integrating Anonymised with Google Publisher Signals](https://www.anonymised.io/blog-posts/integrating-anonymised-with-googles-publisher-provided-signals): Anonymised now integrates with Google's Publisher Provided Signals (PPS), helping publishers monetise their ID-less audiences through Google Ad Manager.
- [Introducing Anonymised Retargeting](https://www.anonymised.io/blog-posts/introducing-anonymised-retargeting): Anonymised Retargeting brings event and campaign-based retargeting back to cookieless, ID-less programmatic, with no third-party identifiers required.
- [Does Google’s decision bring us closer to the demise of third-party cookies?](https://www.anonymised.io/blog-posts/the-queen-sacrifice-does-googles-decision-bring-us-closer-to-the-demise-of-third-party-cookies): Why making third-party cookie deprecation a Chrome user's choice is a calculated sacrifice that speeds up, rather than delays, the end of the cookie.
- [Introducing Anonymised Attribution](https://www.anonymised.io/blog-posts/introducing-anonymised-attribution): Use Anonymised Attribution for Multi-Touch Attribution or Marketing Mixed Modelling as an alternative to those using third-party cookies.
- [Allan Tinkler Joins Anonymised as Commercial Lead](https://www.anonymised.io/blog-posts/welcome-allan-tinkler-the-new-commercial-lead-here-at-anonymised): Allan Tinkler joins Anonymised as Commercial Lead, bringing over 20 years of commercial experience across both the sell side and the buy side.
- [Welcome Chris Clarke, our new Head of Integrations](https://www.anonymised.io/blog-posts/welcome-chris-clarke-our-new-head-of-integrations): Chris Clarke joins Anonymised as Head of Integrations, with experience as an implementation manager, software developer and success engineer.
- [Mumsnet - 1PD to onboard incremental non-endemic advertisers](https://www.anonymised.io/blog-posts/mumsnet-enriching-1pd-to-onboard-incremental-non-endemic-advertisers): Anonymised enriched Mumsnet's first-party data with cross-site behaviour: 4x the addressable reach, a 29% CTR uplift and 3x new non-endemic advertisers.
- [Incremental cookieless reach & performance for global brand](https://www.anonymised.io/blog-posts/hoopla-a-global-entertainment-brand): Hoopla Digital built five cookieless audiences with Anonymised, gaining 83% more addressable reach and a 13% CTR uplift over third-party cookies.
- [Understanding Curation: Pros and Cons of Trading Ads](https://www.anonymised.io/blog-posts/understanding-curation-the-pros-and-cons-of-a-new-way-of-trading-ads): Many are calling 2024 the year of curation. What programmatic curation is, how it works, its pros and cons, and what you can expect from it.
- [The Privacy Sandbox: Imperfect, Competition Steps In](https://www.anonymised.io/blog-posts/the-privacy-sandbox-is-not-perfect-but-competition-can-fill-the-gaps): Google's Privacy Sandbox splits ad tech into two cookieless universes. Where it falls short for publishers and advertisers, and how competition can help.
- [Traders, beware of Muscle Memory Overreach ](https://www.anonymised.io/blog-posts/traders-beware-of-muscle-memory-overreach): Third-party cookies are built into programmatic trading habits. How Muscle Memory Overreach undermines cookieless campaigns, and three steps to retrain.
- [Winners and losers from the last Christmas cookie party ](https://www.anonymised.io/blog-posts/winners-and-losers-from-the-last-christmas-cookie-party): A half-serious look at who wins and who loses in digital advertising, the open internet and the information economy once third-party cookies are gone.
- [Why Privacy Now: 4 Insights After Two Months](https://www.anonymised.io/blog-posts/ginormous-elephants-broken-promises-and-why-now-4-observations-from-2-months-going-all-in-on-privacy): Four observations from two months working on privacy-enhancing technology, including why up to 70% of users already cannot be addressed.
- [To Survive, Digital Ads Must Drop Interoperability](https://www.anonymised.io/blog-posts/to-save-itself-digital-advertising-must-abandon-interoperability): The end of third-party cookies threatens targeting, frequency capping and attribution on the open web. Why the industry must give up interoperability.
- [Anonymised Appoints Isabel González Head of Success](https://www.anonymised.io/blog-posts/new-head-of-customer-success-isabel-gonzalez-joins-anonymised): Isabel González joins Anonymised as Head of Customer Success. We asked her why she joined, what her first months look like and where the industry is going.
- [Publicis Media and top UK publishers announce test of innovative privacy-enhancing cookieless technology](https://www.anonymised.io/blog-posts/publicis-media-and-aop-test-anonymised): Publicis Media and the UK Association of Online Publishers run a large-scale test of Anonymised, a privacy-enhancing technology for cookieless targeting.
- [What does one year revolutionising ad tech teach you? ](https://www.anonymised.io/blog-posts/what-does-one-year-revolutionising-ad-tech-teach-you): Jon Caines, our Head of Customer Success, looks back on his first year at Anonymised and the lessons learned from joining an ad tech start-up.
- [Dentsu X for a premium fashion brand](https://www.anonymised.io/blog-posts/dentsu-x-for-for-a-premium-fashion-brand): Dentsu X tested Anonymised audiences for a premium fashion brand against contextual targeting: 360% more qualified traffic and a 30% lower bounce rate.
- [An interview with our NEWEST member of the team Pete Emms](https://www.anonymised.io/blog-posts/pete-emms-head-of-publisher-revenue-joins-anonymised): Pete Emms joins Anonymised as Head of Publisher Revenue. We asked him why he joined, what he will focus on first and where the industry is heading.
- [GEDI - The Italian Publisher with 3x number of conversions](https://www.anonymised.io/blog-posts/gedi-the-italian-publisher-with-3x-the-number-of-conversions-on-their-inventory): GEDI mapped 80% of its audience on La Repubblica and La Stampa in four months, and advertisers saw 3x the conversions of its prime contextual solution.
- [Anonymised wins I-COM Data Creativity Awards](https://www.anonymised.io/blog-posts/anonymised-wins-big-at-the-prestigious-i-com-data-creativity-awards-evening): We have some exciting news to share with you… The Anonymised team has won The Best Data Startup at the I-COM Data Awards for 2023!
- [The Death and Rebirth of Real-Time Bidding](https://www.anonymised.io/blog-posts/the-death-and-rebirth-of-real-time-bidding): Open-market real-time bidding is running out of time. But RTB is resilient, and offers privacy-preserving paths to economic success.
- [The Battle for Consent in 2023](https://www.anonymised.io/blog-posts/the-battle-for-consent-in-2023): Why consent is still unsolved in 2023: dark patterns, cookie paywalls, problems ahead for the TCF, and how Anonymised is helping to solve them.
- [Rewriting the Rules of Audience Targeting](https://www.anonymised.io/blog-posts/rewriting-the-rules-of-audience-targeting): Why ad tech's use of personal data is out of step with a privacy-first world, and how Anonymised set out to personalise ads without exposing that data.
- [ID Ward becomes Anonymised](https://www.anonymised.io/blog-posts/id-ward-becomes-anonymised): ID Ward is now Anonymised: the platform that helps advertisers and publishers monetise audiences while taking personal data out of advertising.

## Optional

- [Privacy Policy](https://www.anonymised.io/privacy)
